chunks: Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurara said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Is there anything (zakat) upon the mules?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. So I said, 'So how did it come to be upon the horses and not upon the mules?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Because the mules do not reproduce, and the female horses give birth, and there is nothing upon the male horses'. He said, 'So I said, 'So what is regarding the donkeys?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing with regards to them'. I said, 'Is there anything upon the horse, or the camel which the man happens to be riding upon?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, there is nothing upon what is fed (not grazing). Rather, the charity (zakat) is upon the grazing animal sent out in its pasture during its year which the man acquired. But, as for what is besides that, so there is nothing with regards to it'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on zakat for mules, horses, and donkeys in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that zakat is strictly limited to 'saimah' (grazing livestock) that are freely pasturing for a full lunar year, thereby exempting riding animals and those kept in stables. The distinction regarding mules highlights their sterility, while the ruling on horses and donkeys emphasizes that utility (riding) rather than species alone determines exemption. This hadith serves as a foundational text for Shia jurists in defining the specific conditions of ownership and grazing required for livestock zakat.

en.hubeali: Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘Is there anything upon the mules?’ So heasws said: ‘No’. So I said, ‘So how come it came to be upon the cavalry horse and did not come to be upon the mule?’ So heasws said: ‘Because the mules do not reproduce, and the cavalry female horses do, and there is nothing upon the male cavalry horses’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So I said, ‘So what is regarding the donkeys?’ So heasws said: ‘There is nothing with regards to them’. I said, ‘Is there anything upon the horse, or the camel which the man happens to be riding upon?’ So heasws said: ‘No, there is nothing upon what one feeds. But rather, the charity (Zakāt) is upon the grazing ones sent in its pasture during its year which the man acquired. But, as for what is besides that, so there is nothing with regards to it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Hammad ibn ‘Isa has narrated from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if there is Zakat on mules. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, Zakat is not due on it.’ I then said, ‘How is it that there is Zakat on horses but not on mules?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is because mules do not reproduce but mares do so and Zakat is not due on horses.’ I then asked are donkeys subject to Zakat?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not subject to Zakat.’ I then asked, ‘Are horses and camels that one uses for riding subject to Zakat?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, Zakat is not due on whatever one feeds. Only that which is left in pastures land to graze for one year is subject to Zakat, while in one’s possession. Other than this is not subject to Zakat.’”
